key: WE have o’erpassed the limit of this darkness while, worshipping the Gods, we sang their praises.
s: At daybreak a hymn to the Asvins calls the twin gods to the rite; Sāyaṇa, on 7.73.1, reads the darkness crossed as ignorance with its effect, the sorrow of birth and death, or, since the rite is in hand, ignorance of how it is performed.

evidence.words: “अस्य “तमसः अज्ञानस्य तत्कार्यस्य जननमरणवतः संसारदुःखस्य अथवा प्रकृतत्वात् प्रयोगविषयाज्ञानस्य “पारम् “अतारिष्म तीर्णाः स्म । किं कुर्वन्तः । “देवयन्तः देवकामाः “स्तोमं स्तुतिं "प्रति “दधानाः देवेषु कुर्वाणाः ।
evidence.gloss: ‘Of this darkness’: of ignorance and its effect, the sorrow of worldly existence, marked by birth and death; or else, since it is the matter in hand, of ignorance concerning the performance (of the rite): of that we have reached the far shore, we have crossed it. Doing what? Longing for the gods, setting praise among the gods.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 7.73.1 at [588,1]), the first sentence of the verse, which begins and ends a sentence. Sāyaṇa glosses tamasaḥ as ajñāna with its effect, the saṃsāra-sorrow of birth and death, or alternatively (prakṛtatvāt) ignorance concerning the performance of the rite (prayogaviṣayājñāna): the sentence gives both alternatives as his and adds nothing. Sāyaṇa’s preface places the hymn in the morning litany and the Aśvin śastra; plain sense faithful: 7.73 is an Asvin hymn in a run of dawn hymns (7.72.4 ‘What time the Dawns break forth’, 7.74.1 ‘at the break of day’), calling the twins to the sacrifice (7.73.2, 7.73.5); no four-word run from the key. Revision 209146 dated 2019-08-10 by the wiki API. Entry-check ok.
